Subject: Post-demo: ZenBridge integration -- auth, routing, and fallback playbook

Hi Maya / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the clear product context and traffic shapes you shared. Below is a concise recap and proposed plan so we can get engineering moving on a scoped POC.

Quick recap of asks from your side:
- SDK quickstart and auth options (Okta/SSO, private connectivity)
- Model routing policy: low-latency for web, cost-optimized for batch jobs
- Structured output and tool-calling for clinical forms + an embeddings/reranker plan for record-matching
- Estimated throughput: 120 TPS peak for web burst, 50K embeddings/day (rough) — see attached spreadsheet for monthly estimates

Proposed next steps (short-term POC):
1) Tech deep-dive (60m) with your infra/infosec, our infra + solutions engineer. Goal: confirm auth path (API keys vs OIDC + private link) and network topology.
2) POC config: run a small production-like workload for two weeks: US region, latency-first routing for web queries, fallback chain for heavy loads.
3) SDK onboarding: we'll provide a quickstart package (node/python) with example structured output / function-calling patterns and an embeddings pipeline.

For the deep-dive, proposed attendees from our side: Dev (runtime/auth), Marcus (model routing & cost controls), Evelyn (CS/onsite ops). Can you confirm which of your infra folks will be present and a few 60m slots?

I attached an integration checklist and your throughput spreadsheet for reference.

Thanks,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: ZenBridge integration -- auth, routing, and fallback playbook

Connor,

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our infra/security leads:
- Primary tenancy: GCP-US for production; we have an EU cluster for EU patients (GDPR). We’d prefer region-local routing for EU traffic.
- Identity: Okta + OIDC is our standard for auth. For the POC we can accept short-lived API tokens but final must be OIDC or mutual TLS via our private peering (we use Private Service Connect).
- Data controls: all PHI must remain in our VPC for on-prem requests; for hosted we need a BAA and audit logs with token-level tracing.
- Cost sensitivity: embeddings volume will be high; we want recommendations for batching/quantization or routed cheaper model variants for bulk embedding runs.

We can do the deep-dive tomorrow 02/15 at 10:00am ET or 2:00pm ET. Our infra: Samir (platform), Leila Hassan (security).

-Maya
Director of Product | ZenBridge Health

Subject: RE: Post-demo: ZenBridge integration -- auth, routing, and fallback playbook

Folks,

Below is an engineering-first proposal for the POC taking into account Maya's notes. High-level rationale and config fragments included so ZenBridge can validate quickly.

1) Auth & connectivity- POC: short-lived API keys scoped to dev project and IP-restricted; Redwood will capture audit logs and share. - Production target: OIDC via Okta + Private Service Connect / VPC peering. We support mTLS for Private deployments.

2) SDK & quickstart- We'll supply a small repo with Node + Python clients:
  - SDK handles automatic retry/backoff, streaming, and structured output (function-calling) wrappers.
  - Example structured-output contract for clinical form extraction (JSONSchema + field confidence scores).

3) Model routing policy (suggested)
- Routes:
  * web_query: latency-first policy -> prefer region with lowest RTT (US-EAST primary, fallback to US-WEST then quantized variant)
  * batch_embed: cost-first policy -> route to quantized-embedding pool with aggressive batching and cache TTL
  * record_match (high-quality): quality-first -> use full-precision reranker + embedder, elevated capacity

- Fallback chain example (pseudo-config):
  { route: "web_query", policy: "latency-first", priority: ["rwd-large-int8-us-east", "rwd-medium-us-east", "rwd-medium-quant4-us-east", "rwd-medium-us-west"] }

Notes on latency vs cost tradeoffs:
- For web queries (120 TPS spikes) we recommend continuous batching disabled and small-request pools to keep p95 low (< 120ms target). - Embeddings: 50K/day can be batched heavily; use 8s batching windows for nightly backfill and 200ms microbatches for on-demand. Consider a cheaper quantized embedding model for bulk runs and a full-precision model for index builds.

4) Structured output & tool calling- Use function-calling for deterministic clinical form population. We'll include examples that validate against your JSONSchema and fallback to a human-review queue when confidence < 0.7.

5) Observability & SLOs- We will surface token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and a route-level fallback metric. Also propose a canary route for rollouts (10% traffic) before full switch.

Next immediate ask: Connor, can you propose a 60m slot with ZenBridge participants; I'll prepare a focused architecture doc and a short mock routing config for them to review ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
